3454f22e57.q: Why is artificial intelligence fundamentally different from previous technologies like calculators and books?
3454f22e57.a: AI is fundamentally different in that it effectively offers to remove your thinking entirely from the process. Unlike calculators or books which amplify human effort, AI increasingly offers not only to provide power but also to set the direction of thought itself, turning what Steve Jobs called a bicycle for the mind into a motorcycle that can remove the rider from active participation.

48b9df5f83.q: What is the reverse Flynn effect and how does it relate to AI capability?
48b9df5f83.a: The reverse Flynn effect refers to the pattern that began around the mid-1970s where human test scores stopped improving and actually reversed, unlike the earlier Flynn effect where cognition ascended roughly three IQ points per generation. This decline in cognitive abilities coincides with increasingly capable tools, which can accelerate the trend further if AI is used to outsource thinking rather than build capability.

fd49056d49.q: What does Eric So mean by bundles of inseparable tasks (BITS) in the context of AI?
fd49056d49.a: Bundles of inseparable tasks refers to work that consists of multiple sequential steps where AI doing the early parts undercuts the ability to do downstream work. For example, building a financial model from scratch is what enables you to defend and analyze it, or creating presentation slides is what gives you capability to deliver them effectively—skip the foundational work and you lose the ability to do the subsequent productive tasks that build upon it.

6c98e2c645.q: How does the two sigma problem in education research apply to using AI as a cognitive trainer?
6c98e2c645.a: The two sigma problem shows that personalized tutoring generates two standard deviations better educational outcomes compared to classroom learning. AI can replicate this tutoring advantage if it coaches and helps unlock potential, but it must not simply remove your thinking from the process—it should strengthen capability, not replace it.

63e5a4931f.q: What did Socrates warn about the introduction of written words and books?
63e5a4931f.a: Socrates warned that written words and books would become an excuse for people to no longer encode information in memory, leaving them unable to have command of that knowledge. This demonstrates that tools shape their users as much as users shape tools, creating a cognitive feedback effect where outsourcing thinking through technology weakens the ability to think independently.
